text:
Alex (support): heads-up — acme-corp reports SSO broken after their IdP rotated certs. Users get a 403 on redirect to ACS.
maya-support: thanks, can you paste the error and the metadata they uploaded?
Alex (support): their error: `POST /saml/acs 403 Assertion consumer service not found` and our logs show `No matching KeyDescriptor for Signature`
Alex (support): attaching the IdP metadata they uploaded: 
```xml
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme.example">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo><X509Data><X509Certificate>...TRUNCATED...</X509Certificate></X509Data></KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <AssertionConsumerService Binding="..." Location="https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs"/>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
jamie-eng: quick note — `No matching KeyDescriptor for Signature` usually means either our parser didn't pick up KeyInfo from signed metadata or the AuthnRequest signature algorithm/format changed (enveloped vs detached).
jamie-eng: can we confirm the IdP is signing assertions with the same cert listed in metadata?
leo-idp: acme says they rotated to a new cert that only publishes a thumbprint in metadata (KeyDescriptor has KeyInfo with `<ds:KeyName>sha256:abcd...</ds:KeyName>` not X509Data).
samir-prod: that explains it — our SAML stack expects X509Certificate in KeyInfo to validate signatures by default. Thumbprint-only entries are tolerated by some SPs but not ours out of the box.
maya-support: customer insists they uploaded the full metadata file exported from Okta. I'll double-check the file they attached.
Alex (support): here is the raw metadata they uploaded (snippet): `...<KeyDescriptor use="signing"><KeyInfo><KeyName>sha256:abcd1234</KeyName></KeyInfo></KeyDescriptor>...`
tina-sre: we can add a fallback to accept KeyName thumbprints if verification against X509 fails, but need to confirm security implications.
jamie-eng: low-risk path: attempt to fetch the IdP's metadata URL directly (if available) and parse X509Data. If remote metadata has X509 and uploaded copy was trimmed, that could be customer-side export problem.
leo-idp: acme also has an ACS variant with a query param: `https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs?env=prod` — they say users are redirected to that URL. Could our ACS matching be failing because of querystring mismatch?
samir-prod: our ACS matching canonicalizes by path and ignores querystring but we do strict host+path comparison; a trailing slash vs no slash matters. Need to check logs for exact ACS we received.
Alex (support): log snippet: `Received SAMLResponse relayState=... ACS=https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs?env=prod`
jamie-eng: ok so two separate issues: (1) metadata only includes KeyName thumbprint so signature verification fails, (2) ACS URL includes querystring variant but our metadata has ACS without querystring — however we should still match by base path. Strange.
jamie-eng: next steps: (A) ask customer to provide IdP metadata export from the admin UI (full XML) or metadata URL, not just a trimmed blob. (B) try importing their metadata into a staging SP with relaxed KeyName acceptance to repro. (C) if they can't, add a one-off support toggle to accept KeyName thumbprint for this tenant and log it as a security exception (audit).
maya-support: I'll ask for metadata URL and confirm which ACS they expect. Also requested cert thumbprint and a sample SAMLResponse (with sensitive bits redacted).
leo-idp: I'll offer to coordinate with their IdP admin: if they rotated, they might have a dual-key window where old cert still signs authn requests; but if everything is signed with new cert and they only exported a summary, upload could be missing X509.
sso-bot: deploy-check: no current feature flag for KeyName-thumbprint-accept.
tina-sre: if we add a toggle, don't forget to require an audit log entry and restrict to enterprise support. We'll also need a short blurb for security review.
jamie-eng: I'll try to reproduce locally with a metadata file where KeyDescriptor contains only `<KeyName>sha256:...` and see how our parser behaves. If easy, we can ship a config opt-in.
Alex (support): perfect — I'll update the customer with the ask and tell them we're blocking on metadata URL + sample SAMLResponse + whether they use the `?env=prod` ACS variant.
maya-support: tagging @samir-prod and @jamie-eng for follow-up. :thumbsup:
Alex (support): thanks all — will keep thread updated.
